II.|OF THE APOSTLES.|293}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, scrolling foliage with grotesque heads.png|imgsize=140px|fl={{verse|chapter=2|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 4.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō Whitsunday.}}when {{sup|‖}} the daies of Pentecost vvere accomplished, they vvere al together in one place: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2}}† and sodenly there vvas made a sound from heauen, as of a vehement vvinde comming, & it filled the whole house vvhere they vvere sitting. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3}}† And there appeared to them parted tonges as it were {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 11.''}}* of fire, and it sate vpon euery one of them: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4}}† and they vvere {{sup|‖}} al replenished vvith the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 7, 39.''}}* {{sc|Holy ghost}}, and they began to speake vvith diuerse tonges, according as the {{sc|Holy ghost}} gaue them to speake.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=5}}† And there vvere dvvelling at Hierusalem Iewes, deuout men of euery nation that is vnder heauen. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6}}† And vvhen this voice vvas made, the multitude came together, and vvas astonied in minde, because euery man heard them speake in his ovvne tongue. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7}}† And they vvere al amased, and marueled saying, Are not, lo, al these that speake, Galilæans, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8}}† and hovv {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`do vve heare''.}}`haue vve heard' eche man our ovvne tongue vvherein vve vvere borne? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=9}}† Parthians, and Medians, and Elamites, and that inhabite Mesopotámia, Iewrie, and Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=10}}† Phrygia, and Pamphilia, Ægypt and the partes of Lybia that is about Cyrénee, and strangers of Rome, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11}}† Iewes also, and Proselytes, Cretensians, and Arabians: Vve {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`do heare''}}`haue heard' them speake in our ovvne tonges the great workes of God.⊣ {{verse|chapter=2|verse=12}}† And they vvere al astonied, and marueled, saying one to an other, Vvhat meaneth this? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=13}}† But others deriding said, That these are ful of nevv vvine.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The lesson before the Epistle on Imber Wednesday in Whitsunweek.}}But {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Peter the head of the rest and now newly replenished with al knowledge and fortitude, maketh the first sermon.}}∷ Peter standing vvith the Eleuen, lifted vp his voice, and spake to them, Ye men, Iewes, and al you that dwel in Hierusalem, be this knovven to you, and vvith your eares receiue my vvordes. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=15}}† For these are not drunke, as you<noinclude>{{rh||Oo iij|suppose,}}</noinclude>
